newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas stable, most trades for individual month.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas stable, most trades for individual month.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market was busily traded for individual months throughout the summer on Monday, with prompt gas also active, but there was little price movement, traders and brokers said.

Several trades done in May, June, September and October on the OTC market corresponded exactly, or very closely, to trades for the same period on the IPE futures market. The prices were also little changed from OTC levels on Friday.
"People are backing out, selling months and buying the IPE," said a trader.
Some expected the trend towards trading individual months, instead of whole quarters which has recently been the norm, to increase as players become more used to using the IPE futures market.
As well as the focus on these individual months, there was also some interest in short term gas.
There were rumours of problems at Bacton.

Dealers were unsure if these problems related to the terminal itself, or to offshore production, and most believed they would be short lived, but the rumours were seen as behind a rise in prompt levels.
One dealer who traded day ahead gas at 10.20 pence a therm said it was later offered at 10.50 pence, although it was not known if gas traded at this level.
There was interest in the gas year from October, with several offers heard at 12.80 pence a therm chasing a bid at 12.65 pence, but again it was not clear if any trade was concluded for this period.
A St Fergus seller said that the value of pipeline capacity is rising throughout the third quarter.
"Normally it's 0.20 pence over the summer, but now it's 0.30 or even 0.40 pence," he said.
Maintenance over the summer at southern terminals is driving several buyers towards St Fergus, he added, and the capacity cost is rising to reflect the increased demand.
On the IPE, 215 lots were done, with May trading several times for a total of 80 lots and settling 0.075 pence a therm higher than on Friday.
Otherwise there were single deals in each month from June to October and another for April 1998, with prices little changed from the previous settlement.
